pageCache.pageTitle: Nursery Federation - Welcome from the Executive Headteacher
pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Executive Headteacher
Hello and welcome to Cookham, Maidenhead and The Lawns Nursery School Federation website.
In May 2011 we formed our Federation cementing the already strong relationships from the 3 Nursery Schools in the Royal Borough of Windsor and Maidenhead. The three Nursery Schools retain their individual characteristics and uniqueness that serve their local communities but are led by Executive Headteacher - Sarah Cottle and one Governing Body. The benefits resulting from federating include the sharing of professional expertise between staff, increased staff motivation, research into the best Early Years practice, financial savings, sharing of resources and increased influence on local authority directives pertaining to Early Years education.
Our vison in creating our Federation was to provide all our children outstanding education and to establish a centre of Early Years excellence within our local authority that provides training and support for other providers (Foundation Stage 1 and Foundation Stage 2/Reception classes in local schools, pre-schools and childminders).
This is reflected in our Federation motto:
“Discover, Grow and Learn”
This is our vision for all of our communities – the children, their families, the staff, the Governing Body and the settings we support.
Our children come from a range of backgrounds, diverse cultures and experiences, and we value their individuality and their specific interests. Our ethos is to tune into the needs and interests of our children and families providing a relevant and practical play based curriculum that is designed to develop the children’s learning in all areas of the Early Years Foundation Stage. We want the children to be curious, explore their environment, share their ideas and discoveries, solve problems, ask questions, co-operate and negotiate, develop resilience and most importantly be enthusiastic learners who enjoy making connections between life experiences. We firmly believe that these skills will provide children with the tools to succeed in their subsequent educational journey.
We are very fortunate to work with three amazing teams of very experienced Early Years practitioners. All schools were judged as ‘OUTSTANDING’ in their last inspection however we appreciate that no two cohorts of children are the same and that we rely heavily on developing excellent partnerships with the children’s first educators – the parents and carers who know them best to ensure that each and every child reaches their potential in our environments.
In March 2013 we were very proud to gain National Teaching School status and are now part of a Teaching School HUB. Please click here to find out more about Foundations for Learning.
THE FEDERATION
THE FEDERATION

The Lawns Pre-Nursery
In April 2016 The Lawns Nursery School extended its provision to opening The Lawns Pre-Nursery offering outstanding education and care for children from two years old.
The Pre- Nursery environment offers ample opportunity for exploration and investigation through a variety of activities and experiences. The environment is open plan, offering the very best development and learning opportunities to all children. Children are able to move throughout the different areas of the learning environment, inside and outside. We follow the children’s interests and these are supported and nurtured throughout the play based session.
We offer morning and afternoon sessions:
We offer Two Year old RBWM funded, Two Year old 30 hour working family funding places. We also offer self-funded sessions and these are £30.00 per session.
The Pre-Nursery and Nursery School is staffed by Teachers, Nursery Nurses and Early Years Practitioners, who are exceptionally well qualified, skilled and sensitive in promoting the children’s learning and development.
For more detailed information on teaching and learning, assessment systems, policies and leadership please refer to The Lawns Nursery School.
Morning sessions are 8.45- 11.45am
Afternoon sessions are 11.45am-2.45pm

About Us
The Lawns Nursery School is maintained by the Royal Borough of Windsor and Maidenhead, offering free education provision of 15 hours or 30 hours (depending on eligibility) per child per week. All of our practitioners are trained teachers or nursery nurses with years of experience in early years education and are committed to ensuring the best possible outcomes for all children and their families.
The Lawns Nursery School offers 156 places, on a part-time basis to local children. Children can attend any of the below sessions subject to availability.

Registration
Parents/carers may register their child for a place in the Nursery School and the Pre-Nursery once they are 3 months old. An Application Form (see below) should be completed and returned to the school office with a birth certificate.

Starting Nursery
A Home Visit is offered to all new parents. New children attend a nursery visit before the existing children return to nursery. The new intake of children do not all start nursery on the same day. Entry is staggered so that time can be spent settling each child in properly.

Vision and Values
Our school community believes that our vision can be achieved by:
1. Putting the children’s learning at the heart of everything we do to empower children to;
2. Providing a caring and supportive environment in which the contributions of all children are valued enabling them to fulfil their potential
3. Being an inclusive setting that appreciates the uniqueness of the individual child, regardless of ability and experience, and the wonderful diversity of the local community
4. Celebrating the successes of all individuals no matter how small, to develop a committed and appreciative learning community
5. Establishing dynamic, innovative and creative practice based on research into how young children learn
6. Involving the whole community in the day to day life of the school to enrich the children’s learning opportunities
7. A commitment to the professional development of all staff to extend their knowledge, understanding and skills of early years education to build capacity and secure continuous school improvement
8. Maximising the interdependent relationships of all adults and children involved in the setting enabling us to work together to secure the best possible outcomes for children.
Make choices, take decisions and develop independence
